claim: At a7a71921de, Effect.isEffect is typed (u: unknown) => u is Effect<unknown, unknown, unknown>, so passing it directly as an S.declare guard for Effect<Success, Failure, Dependencies> in @beep/schema EffectSchema no longer type-checks.

votes.reason: At a7a71921de (effect main HEAD a7a71921dee10f96e0d617e5895c6445e02a7d56), Effect.ts:230 is `export const isEffect: (u: unknown) => u is Effect<unknown, unknown, unknown> = core.isEffect`. EffectSchema.ts:88 does `S.declare<Effect.Effect<Success, Failure, Dependencies>>(isEffect, effectAnnotations)` with `isEffect = Effect.isEffect`. Schema.declare requires `is: (u: unknown) => u is T`. Spike check against that SHA fails TS2345: Argument of type '(u: unknown) => u is Effect<unknown, unknown, unknown>' is not assignable to parameter of type '(u: unknown) => u is Effect<Success, Failure, Dependencies>' because Type 'unknown' is not assignable to type 'Success'. Baseline turbo check had no EffectSchema errors.

At a7a71921dee10f96e0d617e5895c6445e02a7d56, Effect.ts:230 is `export const isEffect: (u: unknown) => u is Effect<unknown, unknown, unknown> = core.isEffect` (typetest narrows unknown to that triple; changeset: previously `any`). Schema.declare is `declare<T, Iso = T>(is: (u: unknown) => u is T, ...)`. EffectSchema.ts:88 does `S.declare<Effect.Effect<Success, Failure, Dependencies>>(isEffect, ...)`. Effect is `out A, out E, out R`, so `Effect<unknown, unknown, unknown>` is not assignable to `Effect<Success, Failure, Dependencies>` and the type-predicate argument does not type-check.

At a7a71921de, Effect.ts:230 is `export const isEffect: (u: unknown) => u is Effect<unknown, unknown, unknown>`. EffectSchema.ts:88 passes that value into `S.declare<Effect.Effect<Success, Failure, Dependencies>>(isEffect, ...)`. Schema.declare requires `is: (u: unknown) => u is T`. Effect is declared `interface Effect<out A, out E = never, out R = never>`, so Effect<unknown, unknown, unknown> is not assignable to Effect<Success, Failure, Dependencies> and the type-predicate does not satisfy the guard. beep-effect's installed effect@4.0.0-rc.115 still types isEffect as `u is Effect<any, any, any>`, which is assignable to that guard; the unknown narrowing is what makes the same call stop type-checking.

claim: At a7a71921de, Stream.scan takes its initial state as a LazyArg, so Stream.scan("", f) in @beep/repo-ai-metrics source-discovery.ts fails to type-check.

votes.reason: At a7a71921dee10f96e0d617e5895c6445e02a7d56, Stream.scan is typed `initial: LazyArg<S>` (data-last and data-first), LazyArg is `() => A` with no value overload, and the public example/tests use `Stream.scan(() => 0, ...)`. @beep/repo-ai-metrics source-discovery.ts:338 still does `Stream.scan("", (content, chunk) => \`${content}${chunk}\`)`, so a string is passed where a thunk is required and the call fails to type-check.

At a7a71921de (effect main SHA a7a71921dee10f96e0d617e5895c6445e02a7d56), Stream.scan is typed initial: LazyArg<S> with LazyArg<A> = () => A (Stream.ts:7901-7909; Function.ts:204). @beep/repo-ai-metrics source-discovery.ts:338 calls Stream.scan("", (content, chunk) => `${content}${chunk}`). The a7a71921de spike check log is TS2345: Argument of type 'string' is not assignable to parameter of type 'LazyArg<unknown>'.

At effect HEAD a7a71921de, Stream.scan is typed `initial: LazyArg<S>` on both pipeable and data-first overloads (`LazyArg<A> = () => A`), with docs/tests using `Stream.scan(() => 0, ...)` and the changeset stating scan takes a lazy initial state. source-discovery.ts in @beep/repo-ai-metrics still calls `Stream.scan("", (content, chunk) => `${content}${chunk}`)` imported from `effect`; a string is not assignable to `() => S`, so that call fails to type-check.

claim: At a7a71921de, McpServer.layerHttp converts a POST response to text/event-stream Server-Sent Events when the request is a subscription, the RPC response body is a Stream, or the buffered body contains more than one newline-separated message; this conversion was introduced by commit a2c4154cf8 (#7265).

votes.reason: At HEAD a7a71921dee10f96e0d617e5895c6445e02a7d56 the POST mapper does convert with `admission.isSubscription || response.body._tag === "Stream" || hasMultipleMessages ? toServerSentEvents(response) : response`, and `toServerSentEvents` sets `contentType: "text/event-stream"`. That is current behavior, not provenance. The claim also asserts this conversion was introduced by commit a2c4154cf8 (#7265). I could not open that commit (no loose object, no packed-ref, GitHub URL unreadable). rc.115 `layerMcpProtocolHttp` just returns `httpEffect` with no `toServerSentEvents`, and later McpServer edits (e.g. `instructions?` from #8228) also land in the same file, so the introducing SHA is unconfirmed. Unconfirmed exact claim → refute.

HEAD is a7a71921de. layerHttp's POST handler maps httpEffect through `admission.isSubscription || response.body._tag === "Stream" || hasMultipleMessages` (newline byte 10 in the Uint8Array body minus the last byte) to toServerSentEvents, which sets contentType "text/event-stream" and frames `data: …\n\n`. effect@4.0.0-rc.115 layerHttp returned httpEffect unwrapped (no toServerSentEvents). git show a2c4154cf8 is `feat: add v2026-07-28 protocol adapter (#7265)` and rewrites McpServer.ts (~1641 lines); the only later McpServer commit (#8228) is instructions/strictness/titles, not this conversion.

At a7a71921de, layerHttp installs layerMcpProtocolHttp, whose POST handler maps httpEffect with `admission.isSubscription || response.body._tag === "Stream" || hasMultipleMessages ? toServerSentEvents(response) : response` (hasMultipleMessages is a Uint8Array body whose all-but-last byte contains 0x0a). toServerSentEvents sets contentType "text/event-stream" and frames lines as `data: ${message}\n\n`. effect@4.0.0-rc.115 McpServer.layerHttp had no toServerSentEvents and returned httpEffect unchanged after Accept checks, so the rewrite is new in the #7265 McpServer overhaul (a2c4154cf8 / 2026-07-28 adapter).

claim: The professional-desktop ontology MCP integration harness uses RpcClient.layerProtocolHttp with RpcSerialization.layerJsonRpc() and an accept header of application/json, text/event-stream, so it cannot decode SSE-framed MCP responses from a snapshot server.

votes.reason: ontology-mcp-harness.ts:184-198 builds RpcClient.layerProtocolHttp(...).pipe(Layer.provideMerge(RpcSerialization.layerJsonRpc())) and sets accept: "application/json, text/event-stream". layerJsonRpc is jsonRpc with includesFraming:false whose decode is JSON.parse of the whole body (RpcSerialization.ts:208-226). makeProtocolHttp therefore does response.text then parser.decode with no SSE stripping (RpcClient.ts:922-926). Snapshot McpServer.layerHttp rewrites subscription/stream/multi-message bodies via toServerSentEvents as `data: ${message}\n\n` with content-type text/event-stream (McpServer.ts:1610-1616, 1708-1724). JSON.parse of those frames cannot succeed.

The harness wires RpcClient.layerProtocolHttp(...).pipe(Layer.provideMerge(RpcSerialization.layerJsonRpc())) and sets accept to "application/json, text/event-stream". jsonRpc documents "without additional message framing" (includesFraming: false) and decode is JSON.parse of the raw body; makeProtocolHttp therefore does parser.decode(response.text). Snapshot McpServer.layerHttp (OntologyMcpTransport) rewrites stream/subscription/multi-message replies via toServerSentEvents, which encodes `data: ${message}\n\n`. That prefix is not valid JSON, so this client cannot decode those SSE-framed snapshot responses.

ontology-mcp-harness.ts:184-198 builds RpcClient.layerProtocolHttp with accept "application/json, text/event-stream" and Layer.provideMerge(RpcSerialization.layerJsonRpc()). jsonRpc sets includesFraming:false and decode() is JSON.parse of the entire body; makeProtocolHttp therefore does response.text then parser.decode. Snapshot McpServer maps Stream / multi-message / subscription replies through toServerSentEvents, which emits data: ${message}\n\n with contentType text/event-stream. That body is not JSON; the snapshot integration log fails at RpcClient.tools/call with SyntaxError: JSON Parse error: Unexpected identifier "data".
